methodological_rigor.justification: The study is a preplanned subgroup analysis (n=229) of a multicenter retrospective observational cohort (WJOG15421L/REVEAL), which is appropriate for describing biomarker-testing patterns and comparing survival between post-operative recurrence and advanced disease. Strengths include clearly defined endpoints, multivariable logistic regression with stepwise selection to identify factors associated with multigene testing, and acknowledgment of selection bias from non-consecutive sampling at specialized centers. However, no a priori power calculation is reported for the subgroup, no multiplicity correction is described despite multiple comparisons across biomarkers and survival subgroups, and the OS comparison between post-operative recurrence and advanced disease is unadjusted for prognostically important confounders (stage, performance status, treatment era, driver status distribution), which materially limits causal interpretation. Handling of missing data is not described (e.g., 'Unknown' entries in Table 1), and the Cox analyses do not report proportional-hazards assumption checks.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort/subgroup analysis of a prospectively enrolled observational registry, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. The clinical question — real-world adoption of multigene testing in post-operative recurrent NSCLC — is relevant to oncology practice and highlights a care gap (only 43.7% multigene testing; drop-off beyond 3 years from surgery). Endpoints include patient-relevant OS as well as surrogate testing-rate measures, and the findings reinforce guideline-based recommendations rather than change practice. Translational path is incremental: it motivates earlier perioperative biomarker testing but does not establish a new intervention or diagnostic standard.

reporting_quality.justification: The authors explicitly state adherence to STROBE and the study is UMIN-registered (UMIN000046079), with a patient flow supplement (Supplementary Figure S1) that supports an observational flow diagram. Eligibility, setting, variables, and statistical methods are described adequately, though several STROBE items are thin: no explicit handling of missing data, no description of how confounders were selected for multivariable models beyond backward selection, and limited quantification of participation across the 29 sites. The data availability posture appears limited — no mention of a public data repository or shared analytic code, with supplementary materials referenced only via redacted links, warranting a low data-availability score.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript's primary novelty claim — being the first to specifically characterize biomarker-testing status and prognosis in post-operative recurrent NSCLC — is credible and addresses a documented gap in the literature, which otherwise focuses on advanced-stage or newly diagnosed metastatic cohorts. However, the overall testing-adoption question has been addressed by the parent WJOG15421L analysis (Sakamoto et al., JAMA Netw Open 2023) and comparable NGS success/failure analyses (Ariyasu, Nemoto, Sakata, Iwama), so the empirical contribution is largely an extension to a defined subgroup. The survival finding that post-operative recurrence has better OS than de novo advanced disease replicates prior reports and is incremental. Overall this is a meaningful but incremental extension of prior work.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with a logical flow from a well-framed introduction through methods, results organized by subtopic (characteristics, testing rates, success rates, predictors, survival), and a discussion that properly contextualizes findings against adjuvant/neoadjuvant personalized-medicine advances. Abbreviations are expanded on first use, numeric results in the abstract align with the body, and figure/table captions are informative and largely standalone. Minor weaknesses include dense table captions embedded in paragraph form (likely a conversion artefact) and some redundancy between results and discussion when restating the 43.7% rate and the >3-year interval finding.

key_strengths: Addresses a documented gap: first characterization of biomarker-testing patterns specifically in post-operative recurrent NSCLC
Multicenter real-world cohort (29 institutions, n=229 in subgroup) with pre-specified subgroup analysis and UMIN registration
Clinically actionable finding that storage interval >3 years and non-adenocarcinoma histology independently predict non-submission for multigene testing
Clear STROBE-aligned reporting with coherent figures/tables and transparent limitations section
key_concerns: Survival comparison between post-operative recurrence and advanced disease is unadjusted for stage, PS, treatment, and era — limiting causal inference
No multiplicity correction across multiple biomarker-rate and survival comparisons; no power calculation for the subgroup
Novelty is incremental — overlaps substantially with the parent WJOG15421L analysis and prior Oncomine DxTT success-rate studies
Data and code availability not evidently addressed; missing-data handling and PH-assumption checks not described
Generalizability limited to specialized Japanese cancer centers with non-consecutive sampling (acknowledged but not quantified)
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competently conducted, clinically useful but methodologically modest subgroup analysis with incremental novelty; survival analyses are unadjusted and overlap with prior work, placing the paper at Tier 3 (mid-range oncology) with minor revisions to clarify confounding adjustment, missing-data handling, and data-sharing posture.
